slides.texte_overlay:
Little things that make you surprisingly
good at talking to women
Remember the small stuff. She mentioned her sister's wedding last week? Ask "So, how did the speech go?" It shows you were actually listening, and that's better than any line you could prepare.
Ask for her opinion, not her résumé. "Okay, settle this. Is pineapple on pizza a crime or not?" A silly debate gets you both laughing way faster than "So, what do you study?" ever will.
Learn to laugh at yourself. Spill your drink, butcher the name of the dish, lose your words. Just say "Wow. Smooth. Really nailing this." Owning a small mistake makes you look relaxed, not clumsy.
Know a little about a lot. Five minutes a day on history, art or science, and you'll always have a weird fact or a good story when the conversation slows down. Curious people are never boring.
slides.texte_sophia: Know a little about a lot. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. You'll always have a good story ready when the conversation slows down.

slides.texte_overlay: Compliment her choices, not just her looks. "Good pick, how did you find that book?" lands better than another "You're pretty." It tells her you noticed who she is, not only what she looks like.

Get comfortable with a pause. A few seconds of silence is not a disaster. Take a sip, smile, look around. "This place is so weird, I kind of love it." Calm is way more attractive than nervous chatter.
Know when to wrap it up. Leave while it's still good. "I really enjoyed this. Let's do it again." Ending on a high note beats dragging it out until you've both run out of things to say.
